assumptions_invoked: Full EUR 10000 is drawn at t=0.
The EUR 100 arrangement fee is paid at t=0 and included as a charge at t=0, equivalently net proceeds are EUR 9900.
Repayments are monthly at times k/12 for k=1..24.
X is an effective annual rate; monthly discounting uses (1+X)^(-1/12).
Overdraft additional assumption: the full EUR 3000 limit is drawn immediately.
Overdraft duration is assumed to be 3 months because the overdraft is repayable on demand / not determinable.
Borrowing rate 12% nominal per annum charged monthly gives EUR 30 interest each month on the EUR 3000 drawn balance.
The EUR 25 monthly account fee and the EUR 30 monthly interest are paid as charged at months 1, 2 and 3; principal is repaid at month 3.
Open-end credit additional assumption: the EUR 1500 limit is drawn immediately in full.

Repayment is assumed in 12 equal monthly instalments; source-logic: where open-end credit has no fixed repayment schedule, the directive's additional assumptions close the balance over 12 monthly instalments.
Instalment amount is computed using the stated borrowing rate 18% nominal per annum compounded monthly, i.e. i=0.015 per month.
No fees or charges other than interest.
Drawdown timing is unascertainable, so under the additional assumption the full EUR 5000 is deemed drawn immediately at t=0.
Repayment is a single payment at 12 months as specified.
Nominal rate 8% is applied for one year; no monthly compounding is specified.
The EUR 200 broker fee is financed into the balance at t=0, so it is added to the amount on which interest accrues and appears in the single final payment, not as a cash charge at t=0.

weakest_point: The overdraft case is most likely to diverge: the directive's additional assumptions fix a 3-month duration but do not make fully explicit whether monthly interest and account fees are paid as incurred, capitalised into the balance, or settled at the end; I used paid-as-incurred monthly charges, while capitalisation or end settlement changes the APRC by several tenths. The financed broker fee in case 4 is also timing-sensitive because it defers the charge into the final payment instead of reducing t=0 net proceeds.
